title: Server
description: M2: game server lifecycle between panel and agent. The panel decides policy (quota, ports, secrets, templates); the agent only carries it out.

CONSOLE_LINE_MAX_BYTES.description: Longest console line text in UTF-8 bytes. gss-init splits longer output; the panel truncates a longer line instead of refusing its batch.

CONSOLE_BATCH_MAX_LINES.description: Most lines in one `server.console` batch or one backlog response.

CONSOLE_BATCH_MAX_BYTES.description: Most bytes of encoded JSON lines in one `server.console` batch or one backlog response (gss-init's and the agent's), so a frame of console data always stays far below `MAX_FRAME_BYTES`.

CONSOLE_BACKLOG_MAX_LINES.description: Most lines one `server.backlog` request may ask for.

PROVISION_TIMEOUT_SEC.description: How long the agent works on one `server.provision` (image pull included) before it gives up and answers `timeout`. The panel waits a little longer, so the agent's answer always arrives first.

x-messages.description: Create or update a server from a resolved spec: data folder, image (pull or derived build), network, container. Idempotent for an unchanged `specHash`.
Start the game (gss-init configures first). Refused when the server is over its disk limit.
Graceful stop (spec timeout, then kill), wait for `stopped`, then start. Answers when the start has begun.
Stop the game. Answers when the stop has begun; the final state arrives as `server.state`.
Remove container(s), network and, unless `keepData`, the server folder.
Send one console line (stdin or rcon, per the spec).
Recent console lines from gss-init's ring buffer, for a browser that opens the console.
New console lines, batched (at most every 100 ms per server), at most `CONSOLE_BATCH_MAX_LINES` lines and `CONSOLE_BATCH_MAX_BYTES` of encoded lines per batch.
Docker stats for every running server, every 5 seconds.
A player joined or left (from the definition's `players` patterns).
Re-run the `steamcmd` install steps and the `update` hook (state `installing`, then `stopped`). Only while stopped. Answers when it has begun.
A stack service changed state (created, healthy, exited…).

ServerState.description: creating → installing → stopped ⇄ starting → running → stopping → stopped; failures: install_failed, crashed. `deleting` is the panel's own: a delete (or a rolled-back create) the agent has not confirmed yet; agents never report it.

exitCode.description: Last exit code of the game process; null when it has not exited.

specHash.description: SHA-256 of the spec the server currently runs, as sent in `ProvisionRequest`. In `hello`, a hash that differs from the panel's makes the panel re-provision (while stopped).

reason.description: Cause of install_failed / crashed, as in the last StateChange.

services.description: Stack services (M3); empty for single-container servers.

ServiceState.description: Docker's view of one stack service. `missing` = no container (not provisioned yet, or removed by hand).

specHash.description: SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of `spec`, computed by the panel.

reinstall.description: Re-run install (a `reinstall` variable changed, or the user asked).

ServerSpec.description: Everything the agent needs for one server, fully resolved: `extends` merged, templates rendered, ports allocated, secrets generated.

name.description: Display name, used in container labels.

autostart.description: Start again after a host reboot if it was running.

allowPrivateNetwork.description: Let the server's containers open connections to private, link-local and host addresses. false (the default, and what an agent assumes when it is absent): the agent filters the server's bridge in its nftables table and refuses to start the server when it can't.

files.description: Every definition file the spec references (hooks; templates are already rendered into ConfigMapping.content). The agent writes them below the server's spec folder (INIT_FILES_DIR in the container), hooks mode 0755, replacing the folder on every provision.

DefinitionRef.description: Which definition version the server is pinned to.

commit.description: Git commit the definition was read from.

PortBinding.description: An allocated port. The same number is used on the host and inside the container.

diskMb.description: Soft limit: the agent refuses to start above it and stops a running game that grows past it (checked about once a minute).

path.description: Path relative to the definition folder, e.g. `hooks/install.sh`. No `..`, no leading `/`.

InstallProgress.description: Where a running install is. Present only in state `installing`.

kill.description: Skip the graceful stop and SIGKILL at once.

line.description: One line without the trailing newline.

limit.description: Most recent lines to return, at most `CONSOLE_BACKLOG_MAX_LINES`.

beforeSeq.description: Page back: only lines with a lower `seq` (the first `seq` of the previous page). 0 or absent = up to the newest line.

lines.description: Oldest first. At most `CONSOLE_BATCH_MAX_LINES` lines and `CONSOLE_BATCH_MAX_BYTES` of encoded JSON.

more.description: Lines in the asked range were left out to stay within the limits: older ones for a tail request (page back with `beforeSeq` = the first `seq`), newer ones for a catch-up (ask again with `afterSeq` = the last `seq`).

ConsoleStream.description: output: the game's pty; input: an echoed console command; system: gss-init's own messages (install steps, state changes).

seq.description: Monotonic per server for the life of the gss-init process. 0 = a line from the agent itself (image pull, derived build, service start), stream `system`: not in the backlog, never deduped.

text.description: One line, without the trailing newline. ANSI colour codes are kept.

reason.description: Readable cause for failures, e.g. `Install step 2 (download) failed: sha256 mismatch.`

installProgress.description: Set while installing; gss-init sends a `state` event (installing → installing) at the start of every step.

diskBytes.description: Size of the data folder; null when not measured in this sample (it is measured once a minute).
